# HISTORY — `experiments/mjc`

*Auto-generated big-history summary. Overwrite freely; do not hand-edit expecting persistence.*

## Why this substrate exists

The node opens (2026-07-16) from a single motivating question in [`ideas/physical_control_substrate.md`](../../ideas/physical_control_substrate.md): reading a robotics company's imitation-learning preview and asking where a "vanilla" scaled policy is *structurally* confounded. The answer chosen was to fill a gap in the existing ladder — RHM (discrete, known DGP, known latents) sits far from language (continuous, opaque); MuJoCo sits in between as **continuous dynamics with a real command channel**, still a DGP whose knobs (friction, mass, damping, gear, arena, contact) can be set and swept.

**The one fork that governs everything downstream** is stated on day one and never relitigated: this is a **controllable-dynamics DGP**, not an RL-to-SOTA robotics benchmark. Policies are obtained cheaply (scripted, MPC, short imitation); every experiment is a knob sweep against a vanilla baseline, so the deliverable is always a slope or dissociation, never a leaderboard number. This discipline is what let the arc run ~30 substantive experiments in under two weeks without drowning in PPO tuning or seed-variance hell.

## Three foundations, one day (2026-07-16)

Three cuts landed the same day the idea doc was written, each porting an a2a/RHM claim onto real physics: **contact-residual structure** ([`contact_residual/`](contact_residual/README.md)) showed a forward model's residual is an *event* detector — it spikes at the free→contact impact and decays within ~4 steps even though contact persists far longer, i.e. it marks the regime *transition*, not the regime. **Arity on torque** ([`arity_torque/`](arity_torque/README.md)) killed the "commands are generator-confounded" objection with i.i.d. commands and showed the command-blind model floors at *every* capacity — the smallest command-aware model beats the largest command-blind one, localized entirely on the actuated dims. **Operator intervention** ([`dynamics_shift/`](dynamics_shift/README.md)) found the substrate's signature move: shifting the transition operator while holding the task fixed corrupts only the world-model factor, so a model-based agent re-adapts from ~50 *reward-free* transitions while a protocol-matched model-free policy needs ~240× more reward-labeled data. This cut's `replan_every` ablation — the benefit *grows* with how long the controller commits open-loop — becomes the seed for the entire ballistic line four cuts later, and its biological reading (cerebellar reward-free recalibration vs basal-ganglia reward-driven relearning) sets the interpretive frame the rest of the arc keeps returning to.

## The pivot: two negatives kill atom-first verification (2026-07-18)

[`value_shaping/`](value_shaping/README.md) established the stationary control (value re-allocates FM capacity away from a reducible-but-irrelevant field, with an irreducible contact impulse as foil). But [`directed_readapt/`](directed_readapt/README.md)'s attempt to accelerate Cut #3's re-adaptation with a disagreement-directed drive produced two clean negatives instead: a **global** shift gives no scarcity to direct (null), and against a **localized** shift the disagreement drive is *blind to confident-wrongness* — ensemble members warm-started from the old prior agree in the unvisited region, so disagreement is lowest exactly where the model is most wrong, and the drive under-visits the patch it should target. This is a load-bearing methodological turn, recorded explicitly in the README: mechanism-atom-first verification kept either killing the phenomenon or leaving an already-good baseline, so the arc pivots to **phenomenon-first** — build the actual compounding-adaptation loop, then back-translate mechanism from what works, with dissociation-vs-ablation and factored/dissectible architecture as the guardrails against sliding back into RL-to-SOTA.

## The FM↔value interchange, in one arc (Cuts #4–#4e)

[`meta_adapt/`](meta_adapt/README.md) runs the phenomenon-first program to its conclusion across five sub-cuts. The 1-D damping floor collapses to zero meta-benefit (reproducing the RHM anchor) while an actuator-rotation *conflict* opens the meta-vs-multitask gap monotonically — textbook MAML crossover, now on physics. A context latent decodes the task parameter near-perfectly, yet system-ID is orthogonal to adaptation-benefit (knowing the task and being helped by knowing it are different claims). Value-directed identification is a robust scarcity-gated negative (matches a trivial heuristic). Value-shaping and meta-conditioning turn out to be **two separable capacity levers** whose interaction only pays under capacity competition. The arc closes (#4e) by wiring a real reward-driven outer loop that both prefers the informative regime and rediscovers the value signal's support on its own — with a wireheading gotcha (normalize the weight budget or the loop games loss-scale instead of allocation) that becomes a standing caution for later outer-loop designs.

## Afferent and efferent, then their union

[`curiosity_control/`](curiosity_control/README.md) lands the *afferent* complement: an intrinsic reducible-surprise drive that tracks a **drifting** frontier (the benefit is specifically a non-stationarity effect — it ties on a static one) and is gated by value-relevance (tracks off-path structure too, but only on-path tracking helps control). It also surfaces the arc's cleanest negative-result inversion: pure curiosity has a **noisy-TV pathology** on this low-dimensional substrate (disagreement chases aleatoric noise, the opposite of the earlier active-vision result, because low-dim bootstrapped ensembles disagree on noise instead of converging past it) — fixed not by a smarter filter but by **grounding**: explore and exploit as two additive drives with an interior optimum, the `e`-tap/`p`-tap unification the value-loop idea doc had only sketched.

[`online_value_loop/`](online_value_loop/README.md) then builds the keystone both directions live in — a *continuously* live FM, not a batch-trained one — and gets obstructed on **both** levers: CEM-MPC control turns out robust to the afferent tracking effect, and the efferent value-shaping benefit is a slow, commit-dependent, *pre-convergence transient* rather than a converged-competence effect. Framed as a positive confirmation rather than a dead end: **value is a slow/committed quantity**, so the two-timescale split the idea doc proposed is *forced by the phenomenon*, not a design choice — and its payoff is adaptation *speed*.

[`drift_value_loop/`](drift_value_loop/README.md) takes that finding under perpetual drift, three cuts deep, and lands the piece that had been missing: compounding across a drift sequence is real, but it comes from **memory** (a context latent), not from value-carving itself; value-relevance carving is capacity-gated and control-robust; and grading the meta-loop by **value-relevant FM prediction-error** (rather than control) — the literal cerebellum→VTA analogy — gives the explore/exploit balance a clean interior optimum the loop can actually climb. Net: the missing piece across this whole interchange arc was always **the teacher**, not the value structure.

## Ballistic control: the control mode gates transmission

[`ballistic/`](ballistic/README.md) resolves why the FM→behavior bridge kept failing to transmit cleanly: **replanning is a blind grader** — it re-grounds past a stale model every step, so control performance can't distinguish a good FM from a mediocre one. A ballistic (feedforward, committed) controller makes the FM ~3× more behaviorally load-bearing than reactive control, and restores ~4.3× more competence after a drift via reward-free re-adaptation. This reframes the entire arc's earlier "weak control signal" moments as a fact about *how open-loop the controller commits*, not about the value system, and its lead reading (the cerebellar FM is simultaneously the reward-free-maintainable asset and the feedforward-critical asset) unifies the biological story that started with Cut #3. Its child, [`ballistic/directed/`](ballistic/directed/README.md), lands a directed-collection ladder — but also **retracts its own S2 result** as unmeasurable: teleport collection gives probes/monitors a ~22× free-measurement subsidy, so "where should I look" has no real job to do under teleportation.

## Embodiment made real, and the retraction answered

[`on_policy/`](on_policy/README.md) turns "how experience is acquired" into a variable rather than an assumption, via a metered `Body` that never exposes `set_state`. **E0** finds most of on-policy's apparent advantage was a *mistuned teleport knob*, not embodiment — but that command-state entanglement (continuity itself) is genuinely structural. **E1** shows a **global** drift reproduces under every collection mode — a globally-learnable shift is repairable from any motion, refuting the memo's own prediction that on-policy would stretch the recovery. **E2** flips that once the drift is made **local**: on-policy needs 2.5× more transitions and broad teleport never repairs the region at all — embodiment is free when structure is global, expensive when it's local, and *only* the local regime makes "where should I practice?" a real question. [`on_policy/directed_on_policy/`](on_policy/directed_on_policy/README.md) (**E3**) is the direct answer to `ballistic/directed`'s retraction: re-run the same directed-collection ladder with monitoring itself embodied and metered (subsidy 1.84× instead of 22×), and the relevance claim reproduces cleanly across 3 seeds — value beats learning-progress-only (relevance pays) and beats error-only (reducibility-awareness pays; error-only burns 47% of budget on the noisy-TV trap). This is the arc's live thread as of late July.

## Cut #5: a flagship question closed as a negative, and a motivation retired

[`expansion/`](expansion/README.md) finally runs the idea doc's own "single biggest open question," unrun for months: does drifting a plant's dynamics open a forward model's representational frontier? Built as calibrate→measure→calibrate (because rank-shaped instruments had failed three times on this substrate), the answer is **no** — drift moves the target function by ±0.08 directions against a genuine-support-increase calibration of +0.72±0.42, roughly 10× smaller, de-confounded across drift geometry. This directly retires a founding claim in [`ideas/physical_control_substrate.md`](../../ideas/physical_control_substrate.md) — "drifting dynamics is a novelty generator" — while explicitly preserving drift's separate, still-load-bearing role as a *realism* device for the entire value-loop line. The belief this cut was testing ([`beliefs/dimensionality_expansion.md`](../../beliefs/dimensionality_expansion.md)) survives narrowed in scope: expansion needs hierarchical structure to expand *into*, which a fixed-DOF motor plant does not have — the real test belongs in RHM's residual-decomposition line instead.

That handoff is not hypothetical: the retraction of a rank-triple readout that a mid-arc idea doc (`ideas/heterogeneous_graders.md`, prompted directly by this node's on-policy E3 result) had written into cut #5's original spec is exactly what forced the calibrate-first redesign, and the corrected account was published as its own finding in [`rhm/residual_decomposition/`](../rhm/residual_decomposition/README.md) — a case of this node generating a question that could only be resolved a level up.

## Where the arc stands

[`arm_substrate/`](arm_substrate/README.md) built a second task family late (capacity competition intrinsic to the plant rather than manufactured, a passive tool spanning the capacity-competition boundary on one physical knob) specifically to retire the "single family" caveat that had shadowed the ballistic and expansion results — characterization only, no cut ported onto it yet. The live thread, per the top-level README's own accounting, is pushing `ballistic/directed`'s retracted question fully onto the local-drift on-policy substrate and re-testing whether ensemble disagreement — which S1 found structurally unable to detect a drift when every member had data everywhere — can finally do its job once on-policy collection creates genuinely unvisited territory to disagree about.
